author: reek
body: A real webserver: a request larger than one frame is reassembled, a Content-Length body is awaited, and the GET that rides in on the handshake ACK is delivered rather than dropped.

author: reek
body: Client A sends a GET split across two data frames, with NO bare ACK first: the first data frame arrives in SYN_RECEIVED, so this also proves that path delivers its payload. After the partial frame the request has no blank-line terminator, so it must NOT be served (served stays 0); after the rest, it completes (served 1). If the SYN_RECEIVED payload were dropped, or a partial request were parsed eagerly, the count would be wrong.

author: reek
body: Client B sends a POST whose headers declare Content-Length: 5 and whose body arrives in a later frame. After the header frame the body is absent, so it must wait (served unchanged); after the body frame it completes.
